title: California security deposit cap and return requirements
requirement: A landlord may not demand a security deposit above one month's rent (two months for a small natural-person owner), and must return the remainder with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates.
key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months for small natural-person landlords
coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling. Natural-person landlords or LLCs of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties totaling four units may take up to two months' rent.

applicability.per_tenancy: The two-month higher-security option does not apply if the prospective tenant is a service member; the one-month cap does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

exemptions: Advance payment of six months' rent if the lease term is six months or longer; alterations made by mutual agreement; the one-month cap does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024; service members from the two-month limit.
penalty: A landlord who in bad faith fails to comply with the return requirements may not claim any amount of the security.
quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
